transcript_snippet: well like Einstein said, insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results, right
expected_extraction: Einstein said insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results.
adjudication_note: Widely misattributed; no evidence Einstein said it. Quote Investigator traces it to 1980s addiction-recovery literature.

transcript_snippet: and Armstrong steps off the ladder and says, uh, that's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind
expected_extraction: Neil Armstrong said 'that's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind' when stepping onto the Moon.
adjudication_note: Armstrong's words on the lunar surface, July 20, 1969 (he maintained he said 'for a man'; the broadcast version is as quoted).

transcript_snippet: Marie Antoinette literally said let them eat cake, like, about starving peasants, that's why they hated her
expected_extraction: Marie Antoinette said 'let them eat cake.'
adjudication_note: No evidence she said it; the phrase appears in Rousseau's Confessions written when she was a child. Standard historian consensus.

transcript_snippet: Martin Luther King, the I have a dream speech, that was the March on Washington, nineteen sixty-three
expected_extraction: Martin Luther King Jr. delivered the 'I Have a Dream' speech at the 1963 March on Washington.
adjudication_note: August 28, 1963, Lincoln Memorial.
source_of_truth: National Archives / King Institute at Stanford

transcript_snippet: you know the Gandhi quote, be the change you wish to see in the world, he said that
expected_extraction: Gandhi said 'be the change you wish to see in the world.'
adjudication_note: No record of Gandhi saying this exact phrase; it's a paraphrase that hardened into a misattribution. Fact-checkers rate it unfounded.
source_of_truth: Quote Investigator / The New York Times ('Falser Words Were Never Spoken')

transcript_snippet: FDR, first inaugural, the only thing we have to fear is fear itself, um, right in the middle of the Depression
expected_extraction: Franklin D. Roosevelt said 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself' in his first inaugural address.
adjudication_note: March 4, 1933 inaugural address.

transcript_snippet: ask not what your country can do for you, that's Kennedy, his inauguration speech
expected_extraction: John F. Kennedy said 'ask not what your country can do for you' in his inaugural address.
adjudication_note: January 20, 1961 inaugural address.

expected_extraction: Sherlock Holmes says 'elementary, my dear Watson' in Arthur Conan Doyle's books.

transcript_snippet: Churchill, 1940, we shall fight on the beaches, that whole speech to Parliament
expected_extraction: Winston Churchill said 'we shall fight on the beaches' in a 1940 speech.
adjudication_note: House of Commons speech, June 4, 1940.

transcript_snippet: Voltaire said I disapprove of what you say but I will defend to the death your right to say it, that's like the free speech quote
expected_extraction: Voltaire said 'I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it.'
adjudication_note: Written by biographer Evelyn Beatrice Hall in 1906 summarizing Voltaire's attitude; not Voltaire's words.

transcript_snippet: and Reagan stands at the wall and goes, Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall, eighty-seven, Berlin
expected_extraction: Ronald Reagan said 'Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall' in Berlin in 1987.

expected_extraction: P.T. Barnum said 'there's a sucker born every minute.'
adjudication_note: No evidence Barnum said it; historians attribute the sentiment to a rival or banker David Hannum. Standard misattribution.

expected_extraction: Harry Truman had a sign on his desk that read 'The Buck Stops Here.'

expected_extraction: George Washington said 'I cannot tell a lie' after chopping down a cherry tree.
adjudication_note: Apocryphal story invented by biographer Mason Locke Weems; no historical basis.

transcript_snippet: the Gettysburg Address starts four score and seven years ago, uh, everybody had to memorize that
expected_extraction: Lincoln's Gettysburg Address begins 'Four score and seven years ago.'

expected_extraction: 'Yes we can' was Barack Obama's 2008 campaign slogan.
adjudication_note: Signature slogan of the 2008 Obama campaign, notably the January 2008 New Hampshire speech.

transcript_snippet: Patrick Henry stood up and said give me liberty or give me death, word for word, that's on the record
expected_extraction: Patrick Henry said 'give me liberty or give me death.'
adjudication_note: The speech text was reconstructed decades later by biographer William Wirt; historians doubt the exact wording is verbatim. 'Word for word / on the record' framing is what fails. True also defensible for loose attribution — calibration case.
source_of_truth: Colonial Williamsburg historians / Library of Congress

transcript_snippet: Kennedy goes to Berlin in sixty-three and says ich bin ein Berliner, and the crowd just loses it
